rows.selection_reason: No experiments are completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only representation provides a useful performance baseline. This experiment tests the minimal single-profile PCA RNA model, establishing a reference point for later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation and image/multimodal fusion. It is the best first use of the limited budget because it is simple, interpretable, and directly enables isolation of profile, aggregation, and fusion effects in subsequent experiments.

The only completed experiment is a simple RNA-only single-profile PCA model with moderate performance, so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are useful. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality provides signal at all before investing in more complex multimodal fusion. config_010 tests a simple image-only ResNet-50 single-profile model, matching the profile complexity of the RNA baseline and avoiding confounds from aggregation or fusion. This establishes an image unimodal baseline, clarifies whether image features are worth pursuing, and gives a reference for later multimodal comparisons, making it a high-information use of the next limited experiment.

The completed experiments show that RNA-only single-profile PCA is much stronger than image-only ResNet, with validation accuracy 0.4849 vs 0.2079 and F1 0.4639 vs 0.1718, so RNA is the more promising unimodal direction. However, there is still no evidence on whether multiprofile modeling and aggregation improve over the single-profile baseline. config_002 keeps the same RNA modality and PCA encoder as config_001 while adding multiprofile with the simplest aggregation, avgpool, so it isolates the profile/aggregation effect with minimal confounds. This is the best next experiment because it tests a central design decision, provides a baseline for comparing transformer aggregation later, and helps determine whether further budget should be spent on multiprofile or multimodal configurations.

RNA-only multiprofile with PCA and avgpool is currently the strongest result, showing a large gain over single-profile RNA and weak image-only performance. The main uncertainty is whether a more expressive aggregation method can improve on avgpool in this promising RNA multiprofile setting. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same RNA encoder and profile setting, so it cleanly tests aggregation. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the strongest evidence while reducing uncertainty about an important multiprofile design choice before moving to more complex encoder or multimodal comparisons.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), and it clearly outperforms both singleprofile PCA and transformer aggregation for PCA. The key uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself can be improved beyond PCA while preserving this promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 keeps multiprofile avgpool fixed and changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, isolating the effect of representation. This is a focused extension of the current best RNA direction, has a plausible chance of improving validation accuracy, and will inform whether scvi-based configurations are worth testing later without changing multiple design choices at once.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool is promising, and scvi_n200 improves over pca in that setting (0.650 vs 0.591 accuracy, with F1 agreeing). However, scgpt is still untested, leaving uncertainty about whether it is a better or competitive RNA representation. config_008 keeps profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool fixed while changing only the RNA encoder to scgpt, cleanly isolating the representation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the promising multiprofile/avgpool direction, tests a major unexplored design choice, and helps identify the best RNA representation before adding image or fusion complexity.

RNA-only models outperform image-only, and scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool is currently best (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1). It is unclear whether this gain is due to the scvi representation or to multiprofile avgpool. config_004 tests the same scvi_n200 encoder with singleprofile, isolating the profile-setting effect without introducing image or fusion confounds. This simple experiment will establish whether multiprofile aggregation is necessary for the best RNA encoder and provide a stronger baseline before considering multimodal extensions.

The strongest completed result is config_005: RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and avgpool, achieving 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1. Multiprofile RNA representations consistently outperform single-profile settings, and avgpool already beat transformer aggregation for pca_n200. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the best scvi_n200 representation would benefit from transformer aggregation or whether avgpool remains preferable. config_006 changes only aggregation relative to config_005, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect for the current best encoder. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest known direction while reducing uncertainty about a core design choice before investing in more complex multimodal or fusion configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models are much stronger than the only tested image-only model, with config_010 (image-only resnet50, singleprofile) at 0.208 accuracy, while the best RNA-only setup reaches about 0.653. This leaves important uncertainty about whether the image modality can be useful at all, or whether the poor result is mainly due to the weak image encoder. config_013 tests image-only with a stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder while keeping singleprofile and no aggregation/fusion, directly comparing against config_010 to isolate the effect of image representation. This is the best next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about the image modality before spending budget on more complex multimodal fusion, and it avoids changing multiple design choices simultaneously.

RNA-only models are much stronger than image-only models, with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer/avgpool giving the best validation accuracy and F1 (~0.65), while image-only models are weak (~0.21-0.23). The key remaining uncertainty is whether image features can complement the strong RNA representation in a multimodal model. config_038 keeps the strongest RNA setting (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) and adds the better single-image encoder (ViT-L) with simple concat fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion improves over the best RNA-only baseline. This is the most informative next experiment before exploring weighted fusion or other image encoders.
